en.title: Counting Contiguous Ranges with Enough Non-Overlapping Equal Pairs
en.description:
Given an integer array bucket and a positive integer k, count the non-empty contiguous subarrays that contain at least k pairs of equal numbers. Each pair consists of two elements at different indices with the same value; different pairs cannot share an index. So a value that appears c times contributes at most floor(c/2) pairs.

Site constraints: 1≤N≤200000, 1≤k≤200000, -10^9≤bucket[i]≤10^9. The original snapshot marks the constraints as Unknown; the numeric ranges are the ranges this site supports.

Original problem source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/meta#30-enumerating-narrative-sections (fixed snapshot content fingerprint 459167e5e43683da3d3aff6bcd8a7f064a1402d5a7d54d76d8635dc435d41e13).
en.input: The first line contains N and k; the second line contains N integers bucket[i].
en.output: Output the number of qualifying contiguous subarrays.
en.explanation: Track how many times each value occurs in the sliding window, and let pairs be the sum of floor(freq/2) over all values. After adding a value, if its count becomes even, pairs increases by one; once the window reaches k pairs, every end position further right for the current left endpoint also qualifies, so count N-right subarrays at once, then remove the current leftmost element and keep shrinking.
hints: Write a formula for the number of non-overlapping pairs a value that appears c times can provide.
For a fixed right endpoint, the qualifying left endpoints form a prefix range.
